reviewed_decisions.subject: Article page /B order after EC3 Issue #320
reviewed_decisions.review: Retain the sequence check for the beads of a single thread on one page, and retain membership-only comparison when multiple threads share a page. The published phrases conflicted: Table 31 said natural reading order and §12.4.3 said drawing order. Issue #320 supplies the amendment (removes natural; replaces drawing with reading), and ADR 0746 explicitly records the amendment and the reason it selects sequence for a single thread. The residual multiple-thread ambiguity is real because neither the amendment nor the clause orders different threads against one another. The comparison helper has no consumer beyond its own unit tests, so this is not evidence of a rendering or user-visible defect. Table 31's Optional/recommended /B wording still conflicts with §12.4.3's shall-contain paragraph; no parser/reporting duty is inferred from that producer-side conflict.
evidence: crates/pdf-model/src/article.rs module documentation and page_array_agrees documentation
reviewed_decisions.verdict: Retain current single-thread sequence/multi-thread membership behavior. Parent independently read full ADR0746 and article.rs: both correctly explain #320; preliminary stale-rationale concern is withdrawn. Presence wording conflict remains separate.

reviewed_decisions.subject: Article Read tab and activation
reviewed_decisions.review: The UI is an optional implementation of the clause's may-provide navigation facilities. It correctly routes activation through the standard thread-action machinery and bead rectangle. Thread information /I and title are optional; an untitled thread remains representable. Tests cover empty list, titled and untitled rows, activating by object, landing on the first bead's page and FitR scale, and a separately stated thread action. Nothing in §12.4.3 mandates a sidebar, tab name, or a next-bead button.
reviewed_decisions.verdict: Accept as a product choice within the permission; do not characterize the chosen panel controls as normative requirements.

reviewed_decisions.subject: Article producer-corpus evidence
reviewed_decisions.review: The corpus witness assertion was broadened from pdf.js-only absence to producer PDFs. pdf-model article tests include a real pdfbox document and verify thread titles, bead/page links and ring closure; this supplements, rather than replaces, exact fixtures. Do not treat the observed corpus count as an ISO requirement or as coverage of every malformed producer case.
reviewed_decisions.verdict: Retain corpus evidence with its named population and limited inference.

reviewed_decisions.subject: Outline object exposure to scripts
reviewed_decisions.review: ADR 1934 explicitly supersedes ADR 1922's earlier refusal of outline reads: bookmark properties now read from the same model outline and execute through activation; write operations remain refused. This confirms the outline is consumed beyond the UI panel. ADR 1934's reader view still reflects the outline parser's supported projection, not a requirement that the parser validate redundant Prev/Last/Parent links or producer correctness.
reviewed_decisions.verdict: ADR 1934 is the current choice; avoid citing ADR 1922's prior refusal as current behavior.
